meta.title: Nominal vs Real Income: Why a Raise Can Buy Less

hook.text: Your paycheck grew. So why can you buy less? Here is nominal versus real income.
hook.promise: Understand nominal versus real income with one example

design.visualThesis: A growing paycheck and rising prices separate dollars earned from goods affordable.
design.motionGrammar: Matched positions, counting values, opposing bars, deliberate holds
design.assetLanguage: Original vector pay slips, basket and data graphics

scenes.narration: Your paycheck grew. So why can you buy less? Here is nominal versus real income.
scenes.visual: Split paycheck and purchasing-power arrows move in opposite directions

motion.action: Split paycheck and purchasing-power arrows move in opposite directions
motion.cue: So why can you buy less?

scenes.narration: Nominal income is the dollar amount you earn. Suppose your monthly pay rises from three thousand dollars to thirty one fifty. That is a five percent raise.
scenes.visual: Pay slip counter rises from 3000 to 3150; difference becomes +5%

motion.action: Pay slip counter rises from 3000 to 3150; difference becomes +5%

scenes.narration: But over the same year, prices rise eight percent. The same basket that cost one hundred dollars now costs one hundred eight.
scenes.visual: Identical basket remains fixed while its receipt price counts from 100 to108

motion.action: Identical basket remains fixed while its receipt price counts from 100 to108

scenes.narration: Real income adjusts your pay for changing prices. Divide thirty one fifty by one point zero eight. That is about twenty nine seventeen, in last year's dollars.
scenes.visual: Pay amount and price factor form a fraction; result resolves to2917

motion.action: Pay amount and price factor form a fraction; result resolves to2917

scenes.narration: Your nominal income rose five percent, but your purchasing power fell about two point eight percent. More dollars. Less buying power.
scenes.visual: Two indexed bars diverge from100 to105 and97.22; loss is labelled

motion.action: Two indexed bars diverge from100 to105 and97.22; loss is labelled

scenes.narration: Nominal is what you earn. Real is what it buys. Next time you see a raise, compare it with inflation over the same period.
scenes.visual: Dollar tokens move into a shopping basket; final comparison connects pay and inflation

motion.action: Dollar tokens move into a shopping basket; final comparison connects pay and inflation
motion.settle: Compare your raise with inflation, same period

outro.takeaway: Nominal is what you earn. Real is what it buys.
outro.cta: Compare your raise with inflation over the same period.
